thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 decode latency breach detected (hosted-us-west-2). p95=380ms, p99=1.4s, streaming route /v1/generate. Triggered at 3345560000. Paging oncall @ajay.

ajay: I'm oncall. pulling up traces and rollout history. Any customer reports?

ryan: Support seeing ~6 tickets in last 20m, main complaint is streaming stalls / long tail reconnects. One large customer on Dedicated got routed to shared and noticed 30-45s stall.

liz: infra metrics: major pagefaults spiked x5 starting ~3345560300. Heap/resident mismatch on multiple inference nodes. P95 climbed sharply at ~3345560500.

maria: runtime heap/kv-cache telemetry shows heavy eviction churn. On a couple hosts we see repeated munmap/mprotect churn. Samples attached.

ajay: any recent kernel/runtime change pushed?

dmitri: We promoted build runtime-kernel-v2.9 at 3345559000 to 80% yesterday. It included updated TRT/FlashAttn kernels and a compiler tweak enabling loop-vectorization flags. I wonder if memory access pattern changed.

liz: timeline matches that rollout. Canary looked fine but once >50% rollout p95 exploded. Correlation looks strong.

maria: starting a perf record on an affected host (usw2-inf-213). Command:
```
sudo perf record -e page-faults -a -- sleep 20
perf script | head -n 200
```
I also taking /proc/pid/stack samples.

ajay: mitigation options: 1) roll runtime back to v2.8, 2) route traffic away from us-west-2 until rollback done, 3) increase node vm.swappiness / add swap, 4) throttle new streaming sessions. Pros/cons?

dmitri: rollback safest. v2.8 has no pagefault spike in tests. Risk: pod restarts will cause ephemeral stream drops. But much better than 40s stalls.

elena: product: three enterprise customers affected—one already escalated to SE. They want ETA for recovery.

ryan: I'll send a short note: "Investigating streaming latency spikes affecting some requests. We're rolling back a recent runtime kernel change to restore service. Expect intermittent reconnects during mitigation."

liz: p95 currently 360ms, p99 1.3s. Pagefaults still elevated. Recommend rollback now.

ajay: authorize rollback. dmitri, execute. I'll monitor customer comms.

dmitri: initiating rollback at 3345560700. Rolling back rollout-tag runtime-kernel-v2.8 across AZs. Plan: AZ-by-AZ rolling drain with 30s delay between pods to limit blast.

incident-bot: Rollout history for runtime-kernel-v2.9: started 3345559000; canary 3345559200; 50% at 3345559600; 80% at 3345559800. No automatic rollback rule set.

maria: perf trace snapshot (usw2-inf-213) shows page-fault bursts when entering flash_attn fused path. Stack samples point to allocator hot-path allocating temp buffers that are not resident -> major faults.

dmitri: interesting — we enabled fused kernels for mid-length sequences; allocator calls malloc+madvise that may touch non-resident pages lazily. Under load this causes repeated page-ins. There's an allocator-fastpath change in v2.9 too.

ajay: rollback progress?

dmitri: 1 AZ rolled at 3345560850. Observed p95 drop in that AZ immediately. Continuing.

liz: after first AZ rollback p95 for entire region down to 280ms, p99 820ms. Pagefault rate dropped ~40% on rolled hosts.

ryan: customer note update: "Rollback initiated; you may see brief reconnects. We're monitoring and will follow up with root-cause." Sent to impacted accounts.

maria: collecting artifacts: perf logs, dmesg, /var/log/runtime. Uploading to incident bucket.

ajay: any quick non-rollback mitigations if rollback fails?

dmitri: we can temporarily disable fused-FlashAttn path via env var in runtime, but that requires restarts too. Alternatively, route streaming traffic to other regions/old pool; might be slower but avoids stalls.

liz: let's continue rollback. Also open an alert rule: if pagefault-rate > 3x baseline for 5m during rollout -> auto-pause rollout.

dmitri: rollback completed at 3345561200. Full fleet on v2.8. Restart churn done.

liz: region p95 stabilized ~200ms, p99 330ms. No ongoing paging surge. Logging mitigation as effective.

ajay: great. Incident severity set to S1 due to customer impact and multiple accounts. I'm handing off RCA to runtime team. SRE will own adding rollback automation and the new alert. Keep incident open for follow-up.

maria: artifacts uploaded: s3://incidents/INC-2026-999/perf-usw2-213.tar.gz and flamegraph link.

dmitri: next steps for runtime team: 1) reproduce with v2.9 locally under memory-constrained VM, 2) instrument allocator to track major-faults per allocation, 3) revert the allocator change and re-run CI with paging-emulation, 4) add integration test to detect streaming tail under artificial page-in churn. Creating PR now.

elena: product will draft a customer-facing postmortem with mitigation timeline and ETA for permanent fix. Please assign owners and due dates.

ryan: I've noted impacted customers and will send a follow-up once RCA is ready.

ajay: handoff: runtime owns RCA and fix, SRE owns alert+automation, support owns customer comms. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then close if no regressions. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
